items.q: Does GoHighLevel have a built-in HubSpot import tool?
items.a: Yes. HighLevel's help article "Import data from HubSpot" describes a HubSpot Importer that you open from the Import menu on GoHighLevel's Contacts, Companies or Opportunities page. You click Connect HubSpot, log in to HubSpot to authorize it, choose what to bring over and confirm the record counts before the run starts. It handles contacts, companies, deals, custom properties, pipelines and stages, custom folders, notes, tasks and emails, and turns deals into opportunities. The import runs in the background, so you can close the window. When it ends, an import report shows totals, successes, errors and warnings, and the error list downloads as a CSV naming each failed HubSpot record. HighLevel advises switching on Allow duplicates for contacts and opportunities beforehand and testing in a location that is not in daily use. Workflows, forms and email templates fall outside its scope.

items.q: Can I export my HubSpot workflows and import them into GoHighLevel?
items.a: Not as working automations. HubSpot's knowledge-base article "Export your content and data" lets you download a spreadsheet of every workflow, listing each one's name, status, enrollment totals, goal conversions, creator and type, and save any single workflow as a PNG image. The same article says those exports contain no performance data or history and none of the emails a workflow sends. HighLevel's HubSpot Importer does not list workflows among the objects it moves, and HighLevel's HubSpot migration guide treats them as a rebuild: document each trigger, action and delay, recreate it under Automation, then test it before switching it on. Standard steps carry no per-run charge on GoHighLevel, though the texts and emails they send are billed as usage. Premium steps, such as inbound webhooks or Google Sheets actions, cost $0.01 per execution once a sub-account has used its 100 free lifetime executions.

items.q: How do I keep HubSpot unsubscribes when I import contacts into GoHighLevel?
items.a: Plan it deliberately, because the defaults on both sides can trip you up. HubSpot's article "Export your content and data" notes that exporting all contacts includes people who unsubscribed, and suggests filtering on the Unsubscribed from all email property to leave them out. Leaving them out loses the record that they opted out, so a later import or form entry could put them back on your list. HighLevel's article "Importing Contacts and Opportunities via CSV" says a DND (Do Not Disturb) column blocks every channel, including texts, email, calls and voicemail. For someone who opted out of email only, import them without the DND column, give them a tag, and let a workflow set email DND, which is the method HighLevel's article gives. HighLevel's importer includes contact properties but does not say how opt-outs map, so spot-check a few unsubscribed contacts afterward.

items.q: How long does a HubSpot to GoHighLevel migration take?
items.a: Neither HubSpot nor HighLevel publishes a total, so plan around the slowest outside step. HighLevel's guide "Moving Phone Numbers: Migration Guide" puts a port from another carrier at about 2 to 4 weeks for fewer than 50 numbers, and about 6 to 8 weeks for larger or more complex ports. A2P 10DLC registration, required before texting US mobiles from a local number, includes a Fast Track fee aimed at approval within 3 business days. HighLevel's HubSpot Importer runs in the background and can be re-run after you fix the records it rejects. The rebuild depends on how much automation you have, so count your active workflows in HubSpot's workflow spreadsheet export before you set a date. Finally, a paid HubSpot subscription ends only at the close of its commitment term, so start early enough to finish before that date rather than renewing for another term.

items.q: Can I run HubSpot and GoHighLevel side by side during the switch?
items.a: Yes, and HighLevel's HubSpot migration guide suggests a parallel run before you cancel. GoHighLevel's workflows can also connect to HubSpot directly: a New Contact Created trigger starts a GoHighLevel workflow whenever a contact appears in HubSpot, and actions such as Create Contact, Find Contact and Create Association create, look up and link HubSpot records. HighLevel's article "How to Use Hubspot Workflow Actions & Triggers in HighLevel" says the connection works with HubSpot's free CRM. The trigger carries no premium charge, but the article lists all five HubSpot actions as premium steps billed at the standard automation rate, which HighLevel's premium-features article sets at $0.01 per execution once a sub-account's 100 free lifetime executions are used. The published article still carries an internal note asking to confirm which actions are live, so test each one before relying on it. Keep the overlap short: HubSpot charges to the end of its term either way, and GoHighLevel bills by the month.

items.q: Can I keep my business phone number when I move to GoHighLevel?
items.a: You can ask to port it, but texting from it takes more than the transfer. HighLevel's "Moving Phone Numbers: Migration Guide" treats a number from an outside carrier as a port: you supply the carrier account number, the service address, a current billing statement and a signed letter of authorization, and the port takes about 2 to 4 weeks for fewer than 50 numbers. Keep the number active with the old provider until the port is confirmed and calls and texts have been tested. A number already in your own Twilio account follows a migration that HighLevel Support coordinates, typically within 1 to 2 business days. Either way, the guide warns against assuming A2P 10DLC registration moves with the number, so confirm the number sits on an approved campaign before texting US mobiles. Registering a Sole Proprietor or Low Volume Standard brand and its first campaign costs $22.50 once.

items.q: Will my HubSpot email templates and landing pages work in GoHighLevel?
items.a: Not as they are. HighLevel's HubSpot migration guide says to save HTML copies of HubSpot email templates and download the HTML of HubSpot landing pages, then recreate or import the templates in GoHighLevel's email campaign builder and rebuild the pages in its landing page builder, linking each form and button to a GoHighLevel workflow. HubSpot's article "Export your content and data" covers HTML exports of pages, posts and templates, and a separate export of form submissions. Use the HTML as a reference for copy, images and layout, and test every rebuilt page and form with a real submission before sending traffic to it. Replace the forms embedded on your website before HubSpot's paid term ends: the same HubSpot article warns that its forms lose their paid features once the account is deactivated, and that legacy calls to action stop working.
